title: Private child and youth care labor dispute (private care strikes)
reason: Private-employer labor dispute over wage parity, not a documented public gathering or demand for state policy. The cited worker counts are strike/workforce totals, not assembled participants.
notes: Government-imposed arbitration followed on 26 January after a reported health-risk assessment, but the workers’ demand was directed at private-sector employers; no qualifying public crowd is documented.

title: Church-sector labor strike continuing into January
reason: Private/sector labor dispute, not an evidenced January public assembly or demand for Norwegian state policy. The 58 figure is employees in the work stoppage, not an assembled crowd.
notes: The strike began 12 December 2020 and ended overnight on 11 January 2021. A separate 24 December gathering outside Asker church is described in a source but has no reported crowd count and occurred before this unit.

title: Written public consultation on proposed curfew authority
reason: Written consultation submissions are not a physical public assembly. The number of responses cannot be treated as gathering attendance.
notes: The government’s January curfew proposal received 1,429 submissions, 1,255 from individuals, and was shelved in February. This was domestic policy participation but not a protest meeting.

title: Digital demonstration for Russian democracy and Alexey Navalny
reason: The reported demonstration was digital, with no physical Norway assembly or attendance count. Its expressed demand concerned Russian authorities and Navalny’s release, not Norwegian state policy.
notes: Norwegian Prime Minister Erna Solberg participated in the Swedish-organized online action. Digital participation does not establish a physical public crowd of 50 or more.
